To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PEGylated dendrimer-encapsulated gold nanoparticles can be used to track macrophages in vivo by CT.

dendrimer-encapsulated nanoparticles (Au DENP) with polyethylene-glycol (PEG) coating are non-toxic to macrophages and can be used as contrast agents for computed tomography (micro-CT) to image macrophages in the atherosclerotics lesions of apolipoprotein-E deficient mice.

dendrimer-encapsulated gold nanoparticles (AuDENPs), with PEG and fluorescein (FI) coatings, are promising biocompatable nanoprobes for computed tomography imaging of macrophage in atherosclerois lesions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and application of dendrimer-encapsulated gold nanoparticles as CT imaging probes for the detection of macrophage burden.
the application of dendrimer-encapsulated gold nanoparticles (AuDENPs) as contrast agents for computed tomography (micro-CT) imaging of atherosclerosis.
the development of PEGylated Au DENPs as a potential contrast agent for the enhanced CT imaging of macro-phages in atherosclerosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FI-functional Au DENPs can be used as noncytotoxic, biocompatible nanomaterials for the noninvasive CT imaging of macrophae in vivo.
the designed PPEGylated gold nanoparticles were successfully applied as contrast agents in micro-CT imaging of macrophage in atheroscleroitic plaques in vivo.
the designed PPEGylated Au DENPs are promising biocompatibility nanoprobes for CT imaging of macrophaes in atherosclerosis and other concerned inflammatory disesases.
